name: Rotweaver

source.note: The Crooked Moon (Legends of Avantris), appendix A. Numbers are the book's; the words are ours. The book prints the name as Rot Weaver in places.

traits.name: Fungal Step
traits.summary: Ignores Difficult Terrain made by plants or fungi.
traits.text: Difficult Terrain caused by plants or fungi costs the rotweaver no extra movement.

traits.name: Hunting Horn
traits.summary: Carries a hunting horn (AC 16, HP 10, immune to Necrotic, Poison and Psychic damage).
traits.text: The rotweaver carries a hunting horn, a separate object with AC 16, 10 Hit Points and immunity to Necrotic, Poison and Psychic damage.

traits.name: Iron Binding
traits.summary: With iron wrapped round it (a bracelet, Manacles or Chain), it can move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action, but not all three.
traits.text: If the rotweaver has iron wrapped around a part of its body, such as an iron bracelet, Manacles or a Chain (any of them counts as Manacles), it can move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action in a turn, but not all three.

actions.name: Call the Rot (Requires Hunting Horn)
actions.summary: Recharge 5-6, needs the horn. 30-ft cone, DC 13 Con save: 2d10 Necrotic (half on a success) and Poisoned until the end of its next turn on a failure; the call carries 300 ft and kills plants (not creatures) in the cone.
actions.text: Constitution save, DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone, blown on the hunting horn. Failure: 11 (2d10) Necrotic damage, and the target is Poisoned until the end of its next turn. Success: half damage only. Pass or fail, the horn call can be heard 300 feet away and every non-creature plant in the Cone dies of fungus and rot.

summary: A fey thrall turned hunter by rot: it strikes with a staff and blows a horn whose call poisons and withers.
